::: {.why}
Before treating it as an estimator you need to know it is not one quantity but a family, and that most reported values omit the two choices that separate them.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Compute three defensible Sharpe ratios from one return series and explain what each subtracts and how each annualises.
- Say which convention makes a strategy look best and by how much, in your own data.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Compute, for one strategy-like series such as a 12-month momentum rule on SPY: Sharpe with zero risk-free, Sharpe with the bill rate, and Sharpe computed on monthly rather than daily returns then annualised. Report all three and the spread between the highest and lowest.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Add `sharpe(returns, rf=None, periods=252)` to a new qlib/stats.py, with the convention documented in the docstring and asserted in a test. Every number you report for the rest of the year comes from this function, so the convention is now fixed and written down.
:::
:::
